overview: White sets up the King's Indian Attack: d3, Nd2, Ngf3, g3, Bg2, O-O and Re1, then e5 and a kingside attack. Black meets it with ...d5, ...Nf6 and ...c5 for a reversed Philidor or a quick queenside expansion. The play is a slow manoeuvring game in which White aims for a kingside attack and Black has easy development.

white_ideas.idea: Fianchetto the king's bishop, castle, and play e5 with Nh4/f4 and a kingside attack
Keep the set-up the same whatever Black plays

black_ideas.idea: Take the centre with ...d5, ...Nf6, ...c5 and ...Nc6, aiming for ...b5 or ...d4
Break with ...c5 and ...d4 to gain space and cramp White's set-up

typical_structures.structure: White d3/e4 with g3 fianchetto against Black's e6/d5/c5 centre (reversed Philidor)

character.notes: Slow, plan-driven, few forcing lines early; sound and hard to refute. Solid.

structure.notes: Centre not yet decided; White keeps tension and can play e5 later. Flexible.

approach.notes: The King's Indian Attack is a System set-up used against many defences; anchor System.

level.notes: Same set-up every game with clear plans and little theory; Beginner or Intermediate for White.

sublines_that_differ.name: 3.Qe2
sublines_that_differ.how: A more restrained set-up with Nd2 and g3 later.

character.reason: Slow, sound, hard to refute and not forcing.

structure.reason: The centre stays undecided with e5 or exd5 later.

approach.reason: A king's Indian Attack set-up played against almost any defence.

level.reason: Clear plans with little to memorise and a sound set-up.

plans.reason: A g2 fianchetto followed by a kingside attack.
